newsitem.title: NORWAY: Russia's Primakov talks cooperation with Norway.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Primakov talks cooperation with Norway.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov discussed Arctic cooperation with Norwegian officials on Tuesday prior to meeting Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland.
Primakov came to Oslo on Monday for a two-day official visit to the only NATO member country which shares a land frontier with Russia.
He was due to see Jagland in the afternoon before leaving Norway, Norwegian officials said.

Primakov spent Tuesday morning with Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal and local officials from Arctic Norway, talking about priorities in the so-called Barents Sea cooperation, a Norwegian Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
"They discussed concrete projects, such as developing telecommunications and the joint use of natural resources," the spokesman said.
On Monday Primakov and Godal discussed atomic pollution on Russia's Kola peninsula. Norway is pushing for radioactive waste to be cleaned up.
Norway shares a 200-km (125-mile) frontier with Russia in the Arctic, home to the giant nuclear submarine bases of the former Communist superpower.
Primakov also briefed Godal on his talks on Sunday in Brussels with NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana.
He told reporters in Oslo on Monday that Moscow and NATO had made progress on a binding document guiding relations between the former Cold War foes.
At the same time, Primakov reaffirmed Moscow's opposition to the Western Alliance's planned eastward enlargement, which he said could create new dividing lines in Europe.
